Note: This is a remote role based in Pacific Time, with a preference for candidates located in San Francisco.

About The Role

Playground and Console are where developers meet Deepgram for the first time. Our redesigns are shipping into development now, and both surfaces have steady, real UI work ahead of them.

We're looking for a Product Designer to own that execution. You'll work alongside our senior designers on feature-level work, take assigned pieces end to end once the direction is set, and float to whichever surface needs design hours that week. The work is well-defined and it matters: it is the first impression of the product for most of the people who use it.

This role is deliberately flexible. You'll build fluency in our design system, our developer audience, and our product faster than you would sitting on one surface for a year, and you'll be the reason senior designers get to stay on the problems only they can solve.

You'll report directly to the Director of Product Design.

Your first chapter: feature-level UI across Playground and Console, running on Cosmos, our design system.

What You’ll Do

  • Design and refine UI across the Playground and Console experiences, working from a defined problem and a general solution direction

  • Support senior designers on feature work, taking assigned pieces end to end with minimal guidance once the approach is set

  • Pick up design work wherever capacity is needed, across product surfaces

  • Apply Cosmos consistently, and exercise judgment on the edge cases the system does not answer yet

  • Document the why alongside the what, so your decisions are legible to the team and to engineering

  • Give regular updates, present your rationale in critique, and give your peers feedback worth having

  • Use our AI and design tooling in your day-to-day work, and share what you learn with the team

You’ll Love This Role If You

  • Take pride in execution, and care whether the spacing is right

  • Want range early, across multiple surfaces and problem types, rather than one narrow lane

  • Like designing for developers, and find technical products more interesting than intimidating

  • Want to learn from senior designers by working next to them on real work

  • Are excited to move at the pace of AI and figure out where these tools genuinely help

It’s Important To Us That You Have

We care more about expertise and leadership than years of experience.

  • Strong UI craft, with a portfolio that shows clear visual and interaction judgment

  • Experience taking feature-level work end to end, from direction through production handoff

  • Fluency working inside a design system, and the judgment to know when a pattern does not fit

  • Clear written communication, including the reasoning behind your decisions

  • Comfort with technical or abstract product surfaces

  • AI tools already in your daily practice, with a view on where they help

It Would Be Great If You Had

  • Experience designing for developers or technical users, including APIs, SDKs, documentation, or console workflows

  • Exposure to B2B SaaS with both self-serve and enterprise motions

  • Prototyping skills beyond static screens

  • Experience contributing to a design system rather than only consuming one

  • Curiosity about voice, audio, or real-time products

Notice: We're aware of individuals impersonating Deepgram recruiters. All legitimate Deepgram recruiting communication comes from an @deepgram.com email address. If you've received a message claiming to be Deepgram, please forward it to careers@deepgram.com.

This may not be the right role if you’re not excited to experiment, adapt, think on your feet, and learn constantly, or if you’re seeking something highly prescriptive with a traditional 9-to-5.

Deepgram is looking for a Senior Partner Manager to own and grow our AWS alliance alongside the existing AWS alliance team. AWS is Deepgram's largest and most strategic partnership and it spans co-sell, co-build and co-market. This is the third seat on that team, with a specific mandate: build the enterprise relationships that turn the partnership into revenue, starting with healthcare and financial services.

You will work with AWS field and specialist teams and their enterprise accounts, drive joint pipeline through ACE and AWS Marketplace, and pull AWS into Deepgram deals as a closing lever. Internally, you will work as closely with our product, engineering, and sales teams as you do with AWS; co-building on AWS services, enabling our sellers, and making sure what the partnership needs from Deepgram actually gets built.

This is a builder's role on a small team. While our AWS relationship is very strong, there is still tremendous room for growth. You will also own a portfolio of partnerships outside AWS although AWS is the priority.

We also expect you to be AI-first in how you work. Deepgram builds voice AI; the people representing it should be running their own work on AI to do research, account planning, content, analysis, reporting

What you'll do

  • Own a co-sell number for the AWS partnership and the plan to hit it.

  • Build and hold senior relationships across the AWS field and specialist orgs — Account Managers, Solutions Architects, Partner Managers, and industry/GenAI specialists — in the enterprise segment, with an early focus on healthcare and financial services.

  • Source, register, and drive joint opportunities through ACE; keep pipeline hygiene and attribution clean so joint wins are visible to both companies.

  • Transact through AWS Marketplace — listings, private offers, channel partner private offers — and make Marketplace the default path for AWS-aligned deals.

  • Bring AWS into Deepgram sales cycles as a closing lever: funding and credits, solutions architecture support, and executive support.

  • Co-build: work with Deepgram product and engineering on integrations across AWS services, and carry partner and customer feedback back into the roadmap with enough specificity to be actionable.

  • Co-market: run joint campaigns, webinars, events, and roadshows with AWS; own MDF.

  • Enable both sides: teach Deepgram sellers how to work with AWS, and teach AWS teams where Deepgram wins and how to position us.

  • Build the vertical motion in healthcare and financial services. Create joint use cases, reference architectures, messaging, and target account lists

  • Own a portfolio of partnerships beyond AWS

  • Report on partnership performance: pipeline, influenced revenue, Marketplace transactions

What you bring

  • Substantial, hands-on experience managing an AWS partnership at a technology company. Co-sell and ACE, AWS Marketplace, competencies and program mechanics, and the AWS field org as it actually works.

  • A track record of carrying and hitting a number. Co-sell, partner-influenced, or direct quota.

  • Experience selling to or through the enterprise segment. Healthcare or financial services experience is a strong plus.

  • Builder mindset: you have stood a partnership motion up from zero, not only operated one you inherited.

  • Startup experience and genuine comfort in a fast-paced, resource-constrained environment. You are a self-starter who does not wait for process to be handed to you.

  • Entrepreneurial instincts- you find the opening, make the internal case for it, and go execute.

  • Technical fluency: you can hold a credible architecture conversation with an AWS Solutions Architect and translate it for a seller.

  • Strong written and verbal communication, and the presence to be credible with AWS and Deepgram executives.

  • AI-first working style: you use AI tools daily to compress research, account planning, content, and analysis, and you can show how that changes your output

  • A proven cross-functional operator- comfortable driving work through product, engineering, sales, marketing, legal, and finance without direct authority.

It would be great if you also had

  • Located in Seattle

  • Time spent at AWS or another hyperscaler, or managing a second hyperscaler alliance.

  • Experience working with global and regional systems integrators on joint delivery.

  • A strong understanding of AI, speech recognition, voice agents, or related domains.

  • Fluency with Salesforce, AWS Partner Central, and Marketplace operations tooling.

This may not be the right role if you’re not excited to experiment, adapt, think on your feet, and learn constantly, or if you’re seeking something highly prescriptive with a traditional 9-to-5.

The Opportunity
This is a rare chance to support Deepgram's two co-founders, our CEO and CTO. You'll report to their Executive Assistant and learn from her. You'll see how a high-growth executive office runs from the inside, and you'll take ownership of the execution that keeps it moving.


Demand on our executives' time is growing fast. Your job is to own scheduling, travel, logistics, and office operations, so the Executive Assistant can focus on the strategic side of how the CEO and CTO spend their time. As we automate more of the administrative work with AI, more of that strategic work opens up for you too.


You'll also join as Deepgram builds out executive support across the company, with recent additions of executive assistant and business partner roles across several functions. You'll help build the shared systems and standards for executive and cross-functional operations across Deepgram.


This role is for someone who takes pride in getting the small details right and is motivated by knowing their contributions to the larger mission of the company are highly impactful. Priorities shift constantly and much of the work is time-sensitive. For executives moving at this pace, whether the details were handled often decides whether it's a good day or a bad one.

What You'll Do

  • Own scheduling for the CEO and CTO: turn the steady stream of internal meeting requests into a clean, conflict-free calendar that follows the priorities set by the Executive Assistant

  • Plan and manage complex travel end to end, and recover quickly when plans change

  • Support inbox management for the CTO and triage for the CEO: resolve the routine and escalate anything that needs executive judgment

  • Run day-to-day office operations in Ann Arbor: be the in-person point of contact, handle supplies, vendors, and visitors, and keep the space running smoothly

  • Plan logistics for leadership offsites, executive dinners, and team events

  • Keep expenses, reimbursements, and corporate card reconciliation current and clean

  • Use AI and automation to take manual work out of scheduling, inbox triage, and meeting prep, and share what works with the wider executive support team

You'll Love This Role If You

  • Want to learn how an executive office runs by working side by side with an experienced Executive Assistant

  • Get real satisfaction from a week where nothing slipped through the cracks

  • Get excited about using AI to create efficient processes for repetitive admin tasks

  • Like saying yes, asking questions, rolling up your sleeves, and figuring it out

  • Would rather be in the office with your team than support from a distance

It's Important to Us That You Have

  • At least one role directly supporting an executive, with hands-on ownership of calendar management and travel booking

  • Exceptional attention to detail, including scheduling across time zones

  • Daily, hands-on use of AI tools in your work, and real enthusiasm for using them to replace manual steps

  • Clear, professional written communication. Your messages represent our executives

  • Sound judgment with confidential information

  • The ability to juggle competing requests and stay calm under time pressure

  • Responsiveness to time-sensitive executive requests throughout the day with coverage shared across a two-person team

  • Thriving off feedback and openness to coaching. This function is being built deliberately, and you won't be navigating it alone

  • Residence within commuting distance of Ann Arbor, MI, with regular, consistent in-office presence

It Would Be Great If You Had

  • 1–3 years of experience in executive support or a similar coordination role

  • Experience in a support role at a tech startup or high-growth company

  • Experience supporting more than one executive at a time

  • Experience using AI beyond chat, such as automations, custom assistants, or workflows you've built, that you could teach to others

  • Experience with office management or workplace operations

  • Familiarity with executive-support tools for calendar, travel, expense, and communications

jobs.descriptionHtml:

Additionally, we move at the pace of AI. Change is rapid, and you can expect your day-to-day work to evolve just as quickly. This may not be the right role if you’re not excited to experiment, adapt, think on your feet, and learn constantly, or if you’re seeking something highly prescriptive with a traditional 9-to-5.

Opportunity

Deepgram is expanding our enablement function, and we're hiring our first Technical GTM Enablement Manager. This role is the force multiplier for the technical side of our revenue organization. You will own how our pre-sales and post-sales technical teams ramp, stay current, and prove they are ready, sitting at the intersection of Product, Applied Engineering, Customer Success, and Sales.

Our technical field teams run demos, guide architecture decisions, troubleshoot live integrations, and take customers to production. You are not here to teach them their jobs. You are here to make what our best technologists already do repeatable for everyone else, and to get new hires there faster.

This is not a training delivery role, and it is not externally facing content creation. Most of what should exist does not exist yet. You will build it.

What You'll Do

  • Own onboarding and ramp for technical GTM roles, designing and continuously improving a structured program that gets new hires to productivity faster and creating a consistent technical standard across teams.

  • Build technical field framework and playbooks, including:

    • Technical discovery with buyers, developers, and evaluators

    • POC and evaluation standards, including clear technical and business success criteria

    • Architecture guidance for our most common customer patterns

    • Technical handoffs across pre-sales and post-sales

    • Escalation readiness, turning what we learn from individual customer issues into reusable guidance

  • Build and run technical certifications, keeping it current as the platform changes rapidly underneath it.

  • Lead technical readiness for launches, partnering with Product and PMM so technical teams are ready before GA rather than after.

  • Turn subject matter expertise into scalable enablement, pulling what sits in the heads of Product, PMM, and our strongest field technologists and turning it into something repeatable.

  • Partner with Sales Enablement where the sale turns technical, including technical discovery, evaluation strategy, competitive differentiation, and solution positioning

  • Operate AI-first, building the tools, agents, and workflows that let a small enablement function serve a growing technical organization.

You'll Love This Role If You

  • Came up in the field and would rather fix the system than keep carrying the workaround.

  • Are energized by earning credibility with senior technical people, and have the background to do it.

  • Believe in the power of AI to transform productivity, and are eager to harness cutting-edge tools to optimize performance.

  • Would rather ship something useful this month than design something perfect for next quarter.

  • Are passionate about Deepgram's mission to redefine what's possible with speech technology.

  • Value clarity, accountability, and moving quickly without a lot of process or hierarchy.

It's Important to Us That You Have

  • 5+ years in technical, customer-facing roles: solutions engineering, solutions architecture, customer success engineering, technical account management, implementation, or forward-deployed work.

  • Real time spent building enablement for technical teams, not just delivering it.

  • Hands-on fluency with APIs, SDKs, integrations, and developer workflows. You can run a live demo, read a customer's integration and see what is wrong, troubleshoot L1-style issues, and hold a genuine architecture conversation. Production code is not required. Hand-waving does not pass.

  • Experience building onboarding, certification, or technical development programs that people actually finished.

  • Demonstrated ability to get content out of subject matter experts who have no time for you, and ship anyway.

  • Something you have built, a tool, agent, script, or workflow, that permanently eliminated recurring work. In your application, tell us what it was, what it replaced, and what it is still doing today.

  • An AI-native operating model: specific workflows that structurally depend on AI, and a clear account of how you would rebuild them if those tools disappeared tomorrow.

It Would Be Great If You Had

  • Experience with speech recognition, TTS, voice agents, LLM orchestration, or other developer-first API products.

  • Experience enabling both pre-sales and post-sales technical roles, and a point of view on how they differ.

  • Working fluency with scripting or agent building: Python, TypeScript, workflow tools, agent frameworks, or equivalent. You don't need to be a software engineer, just dangerous enough to ship working systems.

  • Strong writing and narrative skills, especially for turning complex technical concepts into clear, usable field guidance.

jobs.descriptionHtml:
Company Overview

Deepgram is the leading platform underpinning the emerging trillion-dollar Voice AI economy, providing real-time APIs for speech-to-text (STT), text-to-speech (TTS), and building production-grade voice agents at scale. More than 200,000 developers and 1,300+ organizations build voice offerings that are ‘Powered by Deepgram’, including Twilio, Cloudflare, Sierra, Decagon, Vapi, Daily, Cresta, Granola, and Jack in the Box. Deepgram’s voice-native foundation models are accessed through cloud APIs or as self-hosted and on-premises software, with unmatched accuracy, low latency, and cost efficiency. Backed by a recent Series C led by leading global investors and strategic partners, Deepgram has processed over 50,000 years of audio and transcribed more than 1 trillion words. There is no organization in the world that understands voice better than Deepgram.

Company Operating Rhythm

At Deepgram, we expect an AI-first mindset—AI use and comfort aren’t optional, they’re core to how we operate, innovate, and measure performance.

Every team member who works at Deepgram is expected to actively use and experiment with advanced AI tools, and even build your own into your everyday work. We measure how effectively AI is applied to deliver results, and consistent, creative use of the latest AI capabilities is key to success here. Candidates should be comfortable adopting new models and modes quickly, integrating AI into their workflows, and continuously pushing the boundaries of what these technologies can do.

Additionally, we move at the pace of AI. Change is rapid, and you can expect your day-to-day work to evolve just as quickly. This may not be the right role if you’re not excited to experiment, adapt, think on your feet, and learn constantly, or if you’re seeking something highly prescriptive with a traditional 9-to-5.

The Opportunity

Deepgram is looking for a Security Engineer to build and automate the technical controls behind our security program. Most of our infrastructure is bare metal in colocation datacenters — GPU-intensive, running containerized workloads on Docker, managed with Ansible, and shipped through CI/CD on GitHub Actions — with AWS used for overflow capacity and a small set of services. Our engineering culture is high-trust and fast-moving. That means controls have to be delivered as code, be reproducible, and produce their own audit evidence — anything that depends on someone remembering to do it manually will not survive.

You will own real surface area: host hardening and configuration management across the fleet, vulnerability and patch management, penetration testing, container security, detection and response, CI/CD and supply chain security, and the engineering work behind our SOC 2, PCI DSS, and ISO 27001 obligations. You will also be expected to use AI and agentic tooling aggressively to punch above your weight on a small team, and to help us secure the AI systems we build and the AI tools we adopt internally.

This is the hands-on technical seat. A GRC and Security Compliance Lead owns policy authorship, security questionnaires, and the auditor relationship; you own the controls themselves and the evidence they generate, and you give that role the technical answers it needs.

This role reports to the Director of Information Security.

Note: as reflected on our published compensation ranges, we are open on level. Strong mid-level and senior candidates are both in scope, and we will calibrate title, scope, and compensation to demonstrated experience.

About Deepgram

Deepgram builds foundational voice AI — speech-to-text, text-to-speech, and voice agent infrastructure — used by enterprises and developers to build production voice applications at scale. Our models are trained and served on our own infrastructure, and we offer hosted, dedicated single-tenant, and self-hosted deployment options so customers can meet their own data residency and retention requirements. Learn more at deepgram.com.

Responsibilities

  • Build, deploy, and maintain security controls across our bare-metal fleet and AWS footprint — access management, network segmentation and firewalling, encryption and secrets management, logging and detection coverage, endpoint security, and vulnerability management.

  • Own configuration management and host hardening as code with Ansible, so baselines are reproducible across hundreds of Linux hosts and drift is detectable rather than merely documented.

  • Secure containerized workloads: Docker image build pipelines, registry scanning, runtime hardening and detection, and secrets management.

  • Run vulnerability management end to end — discovery, prioritization by real exploitability rather than raw CVSS, driving remediation with engineering teams, and reporting on it.

  • Own patch and update management as a program: the server fleet, the endpoint fleet, base images, OS and package updates, firmware where it matters, and dependency upgrades. Set and hold patch SLAs, track exceptions, and automate the routine cases so they do not depend on anyone remembering.

  • Own the penetration testing lifecycle: scoping and vendor selection, scheduling, triaging findings into engineering work with real owners and dates, verifying fixes on retest, and producing the summary we can share with customers.

  • Write detections, tune out noise, and take part in incident response. Improve log, telemetry, and security-agent coverage where we are blind.

  • Run periodic log and access reviews as a standing control, and automate the collection so each cycle produces its own evidence rather than a scramble.

  • Automate compliance evidence collection for SOC 2, PCI DSS, and ISO 27001, and support audit fieldwork on technical questions — the GRC lead owns the auditor relationship and the narrative; you own the systems that make the evidence true and repeatable.

  • Harden GitHub Actions CI/CD and the software supply chain: dependency and secret scanning, action pinning, SBOM, artifact and image signing, least-privilege OIDC in place of long-lived credentials.

  • Apply AI and agentic tooling to security work — triage, evidence gathering, code review, detection engineering — and help secure how the rest of the company uses AI.

  • Provide the technical input behind customer-facing security work: questionnaire and architecture answers, penetration test summaries, and hardening guidance for customers running Deepgram self-hosted.

Skills Needed

  • Solid experience in security engineering or infrastructure engineering with a security focus — enough that you have owned controls in production, not just recommended them.

  • Deep Linux. You should be comfortable hardening, debugging, and reasoning about a large fleet of physical Linux hosts — users and sudo, SSH, systemd, kernel and package updates, host firewalls, and what a host-based agent is actually doing.

  • Ansible at fleet scale is required. You automate first and document second.

  • Strong scripting. Python and/or Go, plus real shell competence.

  • Production experience securing Docker containers and the pipelines that build them.

  • Hands-on experience securing GitHub and GitHub Actions: branch protection, CODEOWNERS, workflow permissions, secrets, and third-party action risk.

  • Experience running vulnerability and patch management as an ongoing program — including the unglamorous part, which is getting other teams to actually ship the fix.

  • Experience managing third-party penetration tests from the inside: scoping them well, and turning a report into closed engineering work rather than a PDF in a folder.

  • Hands-on involvement in at least one formal audit — ISO 27001, PCI DSS, or SOC 2 — as the engineer producing and defending evidence, not only as a reader of the report.

  • Comfortable using AI coding and agentic tools in daily work, and clear-eyed about their risks: prompt injection, secret leakage, and supply chain exposure.

  • Pragmatic. Controls that block shipping without a proportionate risk reduction get routed around, and we would rather you name the trade-off than pretend it does not exist.

Nice to Have

  • Datacenter or colocation experience: network segmentation, out-of-band management (IPMI/BMC), physical and vendor controls.

  • Detection engineering or SIEM/HIDS ownership at scale (for example Wazuh, OSSEC, Elastic).

  • Secrets management with HashiCorp Vault.

  • AWS security (IAM, SCPs, VPC) and Terraform.

  • Kubernetes security.

  • Offensive security background: penetration testing or red teaming.

  • PCI DSS work inside a cardholder data environment.

  • Ownership of a secure SDLC program.

  • Experience with GPU infrastructure, ML platforms, or multi-tenant inference workloads.

  • Certifications such as OSCP, GIAC, CISSP, or AWS Security Specialty.

Notice: We're aware of individuals impersonating Deepgram recruiters. All legitimate Deepgram recruiting communication comes from an @deepgram.com email address. If you've received a message claiming to be Deepgram, please forward it to careers@deepgram.com.

jobs.descriptionHtml:
Company Overview

Deepgram is the leading platform underpinning the emerging trillion-dollar Voice AI economy, providing real-time APIs for speech-to-text (STT), text-to-speech (TTS), and building production-grade voice agents at scale. More than 200,000 developers and 1,300+ organizations build voice offerings that are ‘Powered by Deepgram’, including Twilio, Cloudflare, Sierra, Decagon, Vapi, Daily, Cresta, Granola, and Jack in the Box. Deepgram’s voice-native foundation models are accessed through cloud APIs or as self-hosted and on-premises software, with unmatched accuracy, low latency, and cost efficiency. Backed by a recent Series C led by leading global investors and strategic partners, Deepgram has processed over 50,000 years of audio and transcribed more than 1 trillion words. There is no organization in the world that understands voice better than Deepgram.

Company Operating Rhythm

At Deepgram, we expect an AI-first mindset—AI use and comfort aren’t optional, they’re core to how we operate, innovate, and measure performance.

Every team member who works at Deepgram is expected to actively use and experiment with advanced AI tools, and even build your own into your everyday work. We measure how effectively AI is applied to deliver results, and consistent, creative use of the latest AI capabilities is key to success here. Candidates should be comfortable adopting new models and modes quickly, integrating AI into their workflows, and continuously pushing the boundaries of what these technologies can do.

Additionally, we move at the pace of AI. Change is rapid, and you can expect your day-to-day work to evolve just as quickly. This may not be the right role if you’re not excited to experiment, adapt, think on your feet, and learn constantly, or if you’re seeking something highly prescriptive with a traditional 9-to-5.

About the role

Deepgram is building its decision layer: one governed set of numbers that people and AI agents can act on without re-deriving them. This role builds it.

You are not building pipelines. Ingestion, orchestration and latency belong to the data platform team, and they're good at it. You take what lands in the warehouse and turn it into the layer above the conformed gold tables, the semantic models, and the agent-facing tools that let someone (or something) ask a question and get an answer that holds up.

This is a senior technical IC role on a new team. You'll be the first or second engineer in.

What you'll work on

  • Model the gold layer. Conformed entities for customer, account, project, product and contract. Our identity model spans Salesforce, the console, Stripe and the billing system, with no authoritative key between them resolving that is week one.

  • Own the semantic layer. Author the models that define our metrics once, so a dashboard, a notebook and an agent all return the same number. Version them. Retire the superseded ones.

  • Build the agent-facing surface. The tools, permissions and MCP surfaces that let analyst agents navigate our data without inventing a join that looks plausible and is wrong.

  • Make correctness checkable. Assertions on the things that break silently grain, uniqueness, cross-system reconciliation routed to a named owner. Evaluation of agent output against known-correct answers, tracking accuracy, refusal, and confidently-wrong rates separately.

  • Absorb the questions. Sales, product and finance bring real questions. You answer them, and you leave behind a model that makes the next version of that question cheaper.

What we're looking for

  • AI-native practice, demonstrated. You use AI daily and intricately not to autocomplete, but as a way of working that has changed what you attempt. We will ask what the most interesting thing you've built with AI in the last month is, and we'll go three questions deep on the answer.

  • Production-grade SQL and Python. Code that ships on a schedule, has broken, and was found by your own instrumentation rather than by a stakeholder.

  • Semantic or metrics layer ownership. dbt, Cube, LookML or equivalent owned, not used. You've changed a definition people already depended on, and can say who you told and what the number moved by.

  • Modelling judgement over tool knowledge. You reason about grain and keys before you write the query. You can tell a data defect from an undecided business definition and treat them differently.

  • Comfort in work-in-progress infrastructure. Nothing here is finished. There is no ticket queue to work from and no process to inherit you'll be building both as you go.

  • Clear writing. Much of the output is a definition or a contract someone else has to trust without re-deriving it.

Bonus Points

  • Usage-based or consumption business models, where committed, consumed, invoiced and recognised revenue are genuinely different numbers.

  • Real-time billing and consumption systems.

  • Lakehouse architectures - Iceberg, Athena, Trino or similar.

  • Contributions to open-source data or AI projects.

There is no organization in the world that understands voice better than Deepgram.




COMPANY OPERATING RHYTHM

At Deepgram, we expect an AI-first mindset—AI use and comfort aren’t optional, they’re core to how we operate, innovate, and measure performance.

Every team member who works at Deepgram is expected to actively use and experiment with advanced AI tools, and even build your own into your everyday work. We measure how effectively AI is applied to deliver results, and consistent, creative use of the latest AI capabilities is key to success here. Candidates should be comfortable adopting new models and modes quickly, integrating AI into their workflows, and continuously pushing the boundaries of what these technologies can do.

Additionally, we move at the pace of AI. Change is rapid, and you can expect your day-to-day work to evolve just as quickly. This may not be the right role if you’re not excited to experiment, adapt, think on your feet, and learn constantly, or if you’re seeking something highly prescriptive with a traditional 9-to-5.




ABOUT THE ROLE

Deepgram is building its decision layer: one governed set of numbers that people and AI agents can act on without re-deriving them. This role builds it.

You are not building pipelines. Ingestion, orchestration and latency belong to the data platform team, and they're good at it. You take what lands in the warehouse and turn it into the layer above the conformed gold tables, the semantic models, and the agent-facing tools that let someone (or something) ask a question and get an answer that holds up.

This is a senior technical IC role on a new team. You'll be the first or second engineer in.




WHAT YOU'LL WORK ON

 - Model the gold layer. Conformed entities for customer, account, project, product and contract. Our identity model spans Salesforce, the console, Stripe and the billing system, with no authoritative key between them resolving that is week one.

 - Own the semantic layer. Author the models that define our metrics once, so a dashboard, a notebook and an agent all return the same number. Version them. Retire the superseded ones.

 - Build the agent-facing surface. The tools, permissions and MCP surfaces that let analyst agents navigate our data without inventing a join that looks plausible and is wrong.

 - Make correctness checkable. Assertions on the things that break silently grain, uniqueness, cross-system reconciliation routed to a named owner. Evaluation of agent output against known-correct answers, tracking accuracy, refusal, and confidently-wrong rates separately.

 - Absorb the questions. Sales, product and finance bring real questions. You answer them, and you leave behind a model that makes the next version of that question cheaper.




WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - AI-native practice, demonstrated. You use AI daily and intricately not to autocomplete, but as a way of working that has changed what you attempt. We will ask what the most interesting thing you've built with AI in the last month is, and we'll go three questions deep on the answer.

 - Production-grade SQL and Python. Code that ships on a schedule, has broken, and was found by your own instrumentation rather than by a stakeholder.

 - Semantic or metrics layer ownership. dbt, Cube, LookML or equivalent owned, not used. You've changed a definition people already depended on, and can say who you told and what the number moved by.

 - Modelling judgement over tool knowledge. You reason about grain and keys before you write the query. You can tell a data defect from an undecided business definition and treat them differently.

 - Comfort in work-in-progress infrastructure. Nothing here is finished. There is no ticket queue to work from and no process to inherit  you'll be building both as you go.

 - Clear writing. Much of the output is a definition or a contract someone else has to trust without re-deriving it.




BONUS POINTS

 - Usage-based or consumption business models, where committed, consumed, invoiced and recognised revenue are genuinely different numbers.

 - Real-time billing and consumption systems.

 - Lakehouse architectures - Iceberg, Athena, Trino or similar.

 - Contributions to open-source data or AI projects.

jobs.descriptionHtml:
Company Overview

Deepgram is the leading platform underpinning the emerging trillion-dollar Voice AI economy, providing real-time APIs for speech-to-text (STT), text-to-speech (TTS), and building production-grade voice agents at scale. More than 200,000 developers and 1,300+ organizations build voice offerings that are ‘Powered by Deepgram’, including Twilio, Cloudflare, Sierra, Decagon, Vapi, Daily, Cresta, Granola, and Jack in the Box. Deepgram’s voice-native foundation models are accessed through cloud APIs or as self-hosted and on-premises software, with unmatched accuracy, low latency, and cost efficiency. Backed by a recent Series C led by leading global investors and strategic partners, Deepgram has processed over 50,000 years of audio and transcribed more than 1 trillion words. There is no organization in the world that understands voice better than Deepgram.

Company Operating Rhythm

At Deepgram, we expect an AI-first mindset—AI use and comfort aren’t optional, they’re core to how we operate, innovate, and measure performance.

Every team member who works at Deepgram is expected to actively use and experiment with advanced AI tools, and even build your own into your everyday work. We measure how effectively AI is applied to deliver results, and consistent, creative use of the latest AI capabilities is key to success here. Candidates should be comfortable adopting new models and modes quickly, integrating AI into their workflows, and continuously pushing the boundaries of what these technologies can do.

Additionally, we move at the pace of AI. Change is rapid, and you can expect your day-to-day work to evolve just as quickly. This may not be the right role if you’re not excited to experiment, adapt, think on your feet, and learn constantly, or if you’re seeking something highly prescriptive with a traditional 9-to-5.

About the role

Deepgram's Brand Marketing is growing into a collaborative Brand Studio with dedicated creative leadership, an evolving design system, and clear ways of working. We're looking for a Senior Designer who pairs strong craft with sound judgment: someone who can move work forward independently, knows when a project calls for a fresh set of eyes, and thrives in a studio where ideas are explored together. As an AI company, we're excited about how AI can expand what a small creative team can do, and we want designers who share that excitement.

You'll report to our Design Director and work closely with partners across Marketing and the wider company, turning business needs into polished, on-brand design.

What you'll do

  • Bring big creative ideas and high impact execution. Look to push Deepgram’s creative bar and highlight the power of voice.

  • Take on the full range of design work a growing brand needs, from high-profile concepts like event branding and environmental design to keynote presentations to iterative, production-focused tasks.

  • Contribute to design challenges and parallel creative explorations, and fully support whichever direction the team moves forward with.

  • Drive projects from brief to delivery by keeping momentum, setting milestones, identifying next steps, and surfacing risks and blockers early.

  • Partner with cross-functional teams to understand their goals and requirements, then translate that context into design work aligned with Brand Studio direction.

  • Execute confidently within our design system, brand guidelines, and templates, from slide decks and data tables to campaign assets.

  • Recognize when work is new, high-visibility, or precedent-setting, and bring it to creative leadership for alignment at the right moment.

  • Collaborate with fellow designers, contractors, and other creative resources on shared projects.

  • Stay current as our design system and brand standards evolve, and help put new standards into practice.

  • Use preference testing and other available data to inform design decisions.

  • Use AI tools to speed up exploration, iteration, and production, from generating early concepts and variations to automating repetitive tasks, while keeping the final work to our brand and craft standards.

  • Help the team try out new AI-assisted creative workflows and share what works.

What we're looking for

  • 7+ years of experience in brand, marketing, or communication design, ideally in-house at a fast-growing technical B2B/SaaS company or relevant agency experience.

  • A portfolio showing polished, production-ready work with strong typography, hierarchy, spacing, color, and attention to detail across print and digital.

  • Experience working within and extending design systems and brand guidelines.

  • Sound judgment about when to work independently and when to seek alignment, and comfort escalating early with context and proposed solutions.

  • Strong prioritization skills and the ability to flag competing demands and trade-offs before they become problems.

  • Clear, proactive communication about status, decisions, and risks.

  • A collaborative mindset: you enjoy creative exploration, take feedback well, and incorporate direction accurately.

  • Experience working with cross-functional stakeholders while keeping design direction coherent.

  • Proficiency in Figma (and Figma Weave), Adobe Creative Suite (Photoshop, Illustrator and After Effects), Presentation design software (Google slides)

  • Hands-on experience with AI tools in a design workflow (for example, image generation, AI features in Figma or Adobe, or AI-assisted copy and layout), and a good sense of where they help and where human craft matters most.

  • Curiosity about how AI is changing creative work, and the ability to adapt processes as the tools evolve.

How we work

We work as a collaborative studio. Multiple designers may explore the same problem, and projects often have several contributors. We measure success by craft, judgment, reliability, and collaboration, not by whose concept gets picked. Regular check-ins with your manager keep priorities clear and support your growth.

Notice: We're aware of individuals impersonating Deepgram recruiters. All legitimate Deepgram recruiting communication comes from an @deepgram.com email address. If you've received a message claiming to be Deepgram, please forward it to careers@deepgram.com.
